newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai aims at keeping unemployment under 3 pct.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai aims at keeping unemployment under 3 pct.

text.p: Shanghai believes it can keep its unemployment rate under three percent over the next four years provided it maintains economic growth of at least 11 percent each year, the China Daily Business Weekly said on Sunday.
Shanghai, China's largest industrial city, has drawn up a plan which envisages its economy growing by an annual 12 percent in the 1996-2000 Ninth Five-Year Plan, the newspaper said.

This growth rate would allow the city to maintain a balance between supply and demand of the urban work force while providing jobs for a floating population of around 1.2 million workers from outside the city, the newspaper said.
According to official figures, Shanghai had an unemployment rate of 2.7 percent at the end of 1995, or 144,000 unemployed people. Figures for 1996 were not available.
But analysts say the figures exclude large numbers of unemployed people who have been laid off by state-run firms and who are not able to find a new job immediately.
